body.p: Status of the Application
Claims 1, 9, and 20 are amended. Claims 4-5 and 12-13 are cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer. Accordingly, claims 1, 6-9, and 14-20 are pending.
Support for the amendments may be found throughout the original disclose, for example, previously presented claims 4-5 of the previously presented claims. Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 112
Claims 4 and 12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) as failing to allegedly comply with the written description requirement.
Claims 1, 4-9, and 12-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being allegedly indefinite.
Applicant respectively submits that the claims have been amended and these rejections are moot in view of the amendments.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the claim rejections be withdrawn. Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103

Claims 1, 4-9, and 12-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over PUBG Mobile as evidenced by "[PUBG MOBILE] (noted on the IDS filed 3/30/2023 NPL 2; hereinafter Mobile) in view of PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds as evidenced by "Molotov Cocktail" (hereinafter "Cocktail") and Wowpedia "Damage over Time" (hereinafter "Wowpedia").
Claim 1 recites:
A virtual prop control method, performed by an electronic device, the method
comprising:
displaying, in a target game application, a target virtual throw prop controlled by
a first virtual operation object;
controlling the first virtual operation object to throw the target virtual throw prop,
a target throw operation being used for throwing the target virtual throw prop;
setting a target region in the target game application as a region surrounding a
point at which the target virtual throw prop is thrown,

wherein the target region is set to reduce hit points of at least one target virtual operation object located in the target region for a first predetermined duration, and wherein the first virtual operation object and the at least one target virtual operation object respectively belong to different virtual operation object sets;
based on a second virtual operation object being set to continuously lose hit points
within a second predetermined duration before entering the target region, canceling said
continuous loss of the hit points of the second virtual operation object within the
second predetermined duration upon the second virtual operation object entering
the target region;
reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object at a
predetermined rate within a third predetermined duration after the second virtual
operation object enters the target region; and
based on the second virtual operation object being set to continuously lose the hit
points within the second predetermined duration before entering the target region, re- staring continuously reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object
for a target duration after the second virtual operation object exits the target region, wherein the target duration is a sum of the second predetermined duration and a remaining duration, and
wherein the remaining duration is the remaining duration in the second predetermined duration when the second virtual operation object enters the
target region.
Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references, Mobile, Cocktail, and
Wowpedia, alone or in combination fail to disclose at least "canceling said continuous loss of the
hit points of the second virtual operation object within the second predetermined duration upon
the second virtual operation object entering the target region; reducing the hit points of the
second virtual operation object at a predetermined rate within a third predetermined duration
after the second virtual operation object enters the target region, ... re-staring continuously
reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object for a target duration after the second
virtual operation object exits the target region, wherein the target duration is a sum of the second

predetermined duration and a remaining duration, and wherein the remaining duration is the remaining duration in the second predetermined duration when the second virtual operation object enters the target region," as recited in claim 1.

The Wowpedia reference states that "a 15 second DoT can be extended when it has less than 4.5 seconds remaining at no duration loss (the full normal duration is added to the remaining duration)." Therefore, Wowpedia reference merely provides for an extension of the period when a player loses points. However, at no point does the Wowpedia reference discuss or disclose canceling a continuous loss of the hit points when a foe enters a target region and re- staring continuously reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object for a target duration after the foe exits the target region.
The other cited references fail to remedy the above-mentioned deficiencies.

Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references, Mobile, Cocktail, and Wowpedia, alone or in combination fail to disclose at least "canceling said continuous loss of the hit points of the second virtual operation object within the second predetermined duration upon the second virtual operation object entering the target region; reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object at a predetermined rate within a third predetermined duration after the second virtual operation object enters the target region, ... re-staring continuously reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object for a target duration after the second virtual operation object exits the target region, wherein the target duration is a sum of the second predetermined duration and a remaining duration, and wherein the remaining duration is the remaining duration in the second predetermined duration when the second virtual operation object enters the target region," as recited in claim 1.
For at least the reasons stated above, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1, and all claims dependent therefrom are patentable.
Since claims 9 and 20 recite subject matter similar to but not necessarily co-extensive
with the subject matter of claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 9 and 20 and all the claims dependent therefrom are patentable for at least the same reasons as claim 1. Conclusion

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
